Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failure in the test `testAxisPreceding` relates to the node() implementation in the DOM model, specifically in the class DOMNodePointer.java around line 120.

The relevant method is `DOMNodePointer.testNode(Node node, NodeTest test)` at line 117+. The problematic code fragment is within the case `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE`. The existing implementation returns true only if the node's type is ELEMENT_NODE or DOCUMENT_NODE:

```
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE :
    return nodeType == Node.ELEMENT_NODE || nodeType == Node.DOCUMENT_NODE;
```

This means only elements and document nodes match the node() test, but the XPath node() function is supposed to match *any* type of node (element, text, comment, etc.), not just elements or the document node.

The bug report suggests to fix this by returning `true` for this case, so all nodes pass the node() test as expected:

```
case Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE :
    return true;
```

Because the test `testAxisPreceding()` fails (likely due to node() wrongly excluding some nodes like text nodes or comments), this confirms that the current restrictive logic causes the test failure. The `node()[3]` part expects a node anywhere in that axis, any node kind, so restricting to elements and document nodes is incorrect.

Hence, the root cause is the logic in `DOMNodePointer.testNode(Node, NodeTest)` at the case `Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE` only matching elements and document nodes rather than all nodes.

This diagnosis aligns with the bug report's suggestion and the test failure symptoms.

The issue is within the DOM model's implementation; a similar issue might exist in JDOMNodePointer per the report.

Next, it would be good to check if there is a similar method in JDOMNodePointer for analogous correction.
